spec_match.rationale: Targets the §3.1.6 keyboard contract precisely — sequential tab stops in links mode versus roving focusgroup in tabs mode — with the spec's expectations reproduced in a comparison table beside two live carousels declared with each mode.

interactive.rationale: A start-walk button, real focusin/keydown journaling with per-lane tallies, a clear control, and live markers users can Tab and arrow through.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index promises a live journal of which element holds focus and which keys move it; the page records exactly that.

edge_cases.rationale: Handles the same-behaviour fallback on pre-modes browsers and explains the marker-of(...) activeElement aliasing, but cannot journal the activation-focus difference (sequential-focus starting point vs focus-retained) without a real user gesture.

references.rationale: chromestatus link, the modes section, and the activation-behavior section are all cited.

conformance.rationale: The keyboard/role contract this page observes is pinned in the feature suite as the manual tabs-mode-aria-contract assertion; the scriptable grammar assertions cover the declarations the two lanes use.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 evidence: markers render in both lanes, the autorun programmatic walk recorded 2 focus entries in the journal, console clean, mobile emulation shows no overflow. Real Tab/arrow traversal of pseudo-element markers requires trusted key events a headless dump cannot synthesise, and 141 will journal identical behaviour for both lanes anyway — recorded honestly in the banner.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts the support probe, fallback branch, and that the autorun walk recorded journal entries; journal writes are bounded to 60 rows.

design_system.rationale: Variables only, the journal is a bordered mono list with AA contrast, marker active state inverts both colours, group strips have explicit heights.

accessibility.rationale: The journal is a role=log region with a labelled heading, tallies are announced via aria-live output, both carousels carry aria-labels, and the page is explicit about what document.activeElement can and cannot reveal about pseudo-element focus.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: CDP-emulated 360x740 DPR3: zero horizontal overflow, no console errors; lanes stack via auto-fit grid.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Focus management must be observable and testable: visible focus, predictable order, and text equivalents for state.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The page turns focus order itself into visible, textual evidence (the journal + tallies), applies :focus-visible outlines to markers, and cross-references the spec's expected order per mode.

guidanceConsulted.query: CSS-only carousel with scroll markers tabs accessibility
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Tabs-pattern indicator groups should avoid the tab-trap of many sequential stops; roving focus is the expected pattern.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: That distinction is the page's subject: the comparison table states it and the journal lets a keyboard user measure it on their own browser.

openQuestions.title: Capture a modes-enabled journal transcript as reference output
openQuestions.detail: On Chrome 154 or Canary with CSSScrollMarkerGroupModes, perform the documented walk (Tab into links lane, Tab across markers; Tab into tabs lane, arrows between markers, Tab into the panel) and record the journal transcript. Embedding that reference transcript next to the live journal would let visitors on older browsers see the expected v154 output alongside their own.

openQuestions.title: Journal the activation-focus difference
openQuestions.detail: §3.1.9's activation split (links: sequential-focus starting point moves to target, marker loses focus; tabs: focus retained on marker) is described in the table but not journalled, because it needs a real user activation on a marker. Extend the journal to timestamp focus position immediately after a marker click to capture this once a modes build is available.

summary: Instrumented comparison of the links and tabs keyboard contracts: two identically-populated carousels differing only in mode, with a real focus/key journal and the spec's expectations tabulated. On the Chromium 141 build box the lanes behave identically (pre-modes default) and the banner says so; the journal, tallies, autorun walk and layouts verified clean headless on desktop and emulated mobile.
